title: Habitual and actual righteousness as good fruit
source_text: X. Sicut autem arbor mala fert fructus malos, & arbor bona bonos fructus pro-ducit, ita fideles per Christi gratiam renovati & sanctificati, & justitia jam descripta donati, edunt bona & sancta opera, quae in Scriptura quoque justitiae nomine ve-niunt; ut quum dicit Joannes, Qui facit justitiam justus est sicut ipse justus est, 1 Joh. 3. 7. Et Christus ipse discipulis suis, Dico vobis, quod nisi abundaverit ju-stitia vestra plusquam Scribarum & Pharisaeorum, non intrabitis in regnum caelo-rum, Matth. 5. 20. Et prior illa quidem justitia habitualis, posterior actualis in Scho-lis appellatur.
pass_a_gloss: But as a bad tree bears bad fruit and a good tree produces good fruit, so believers renewed and sanctified by Christ's grace and endowed with the righteousness already described put forth good and holy works, which in Scripture also come under the name of righteousness; as when John says, He who does righteousness is righteous, even as he is righteous (1 John 3:7). And Christ himself to his disciples: I say to you that unless your righteousness abounds more than that of the scribes and Pharisees, you will not enter the kingdom of heaven (Matthew 5:20). And the former righteousness is called habitual in the schools, the latter actual.
pass_b_english: As a good tree bears good fruit, the renewed bear holy works also called righteousness.
Schools call the former habitual, the latter actual justice.

choices.why: Key lemma for De Justitia densify §1044.
